Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

society noun

an association, a club

also club, clubs, association, join a society, learned society

classical

Cic. Sen. 45: sodālitātēs autem mē quaestōre cōnstitūtae sunt
M-O s.v. organization, society, association

sodālitās, sodālitātis f.

noun, third declension

a society, a club: a circle of members who meet

Lewis & Short: a society, an association of any kind, especially for religious purposes; also a dining club. Its members are sodālēs (see member). The senate once dissolved the political clubs (Cic. Q. Fr. 2.3.5, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • collēgium, collēgiī n. — an association of people with one calling: a guild, a college

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.27.5: mercātōrum collēgium īnstituere

    A body of colleagues bound by common rules: priests, magistrates, merchants, craftsmen.

  • circulus, circulī m. — a club

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. organization: club

    Classically a circle of people gathered to talk (see group); Morgan–Owens uses it for a club.

  • sodālicium, sodāliciī n. — a club, fellowship

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 293

Examples

  • Sodālitātēs autem mē quaestōre cōnstitūtae sunt sacrīs Īdaeīs Magnae Mātris acceptīs. Epulābar igitur cum sodālibus omnīnō modicē.

    Clubs were founded when I was quaestor, when the Idaean rites of the Great Mother were taken up. So I used to dine with my fellow members, quite moderately.Cic. Sen. 45

See also member, organization, group, president, society.
